articleTitle: Interpretable Predictive Modeling for Smoking and Drinking Behavior using SHAP and LIME
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Current Trends in Advanced Computing (ICCTAC)
abstract: Smoking and excessive alcohol consumption remain pressing public health issues. This research aimed to develop Machine Learning (ML) models leveraging sensor and biomarker data to predict smoking and drinking behaviors for targeted interventions. The Smoking and Drinking dataset (sourced from Kaggle) created from wearable sensor readings, blood tests, and lifestyle self-reports is used to train the 10 Machine Learning (ML) algorithms and validated for smoking and drinking prediction. The Random Forest model outperformed others, reaching an accuracy of 79.65% in predicting smoking, while the XGBoost model achieved a notable 73.96% accuracy in predicting drinking status. Overall, the ML models demonstrate strong capabilities for real-time smoking and drinking prediction using biological data. Such predictive analytics hold promise for early risk detection, personalized care, and nuanced interventions by healthcare systems. This research investigated ML algorithms to uncover and analyze patterns in lifestyle behaviors and associated health outcomes. Additionally, this work unlocks the Blackbox nature of ML models using Explainable AI tools “SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations)” and “LIME (Local interpretable model-agnostic explanations)”.

articleTitle: High Performance Optimized and Unified Bus Monitor for Distributed Avionics Architecture Validation Under Hardware-in-Loop Simulation Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Current Trends in Advanced Computing (ICCTAC)
abstract: The Avionics system of the aerospace and defense industry designed with complex distributed architecture. Every system is intelligent and processing data on it's own. The subsystems communicate with the onboard computer which is the main unit of avionics system. This data exchange is based mostly on serial communication with a maximum rate of 1 Mbps. Many data communication protocols are available; among them most popular is the MIL-STD-1553 because of dual redundant and simple architecture. The data traffic on the MIL-STD 1553 bus is monitored and recorded on the Bus Monitor. The configuration was one Bus Monitor for one communication node. In the case of multi-mode avionics configuration more than one Bus-Monitor is essential to integrate. These Bus Monitor configured separately with no synchronization among them. The development of a single computer-based multi-node optimized Bus Monitor for distributed architecture is designed and developed. The new design and development process of optimized multi-mode Bus Monitor under the real time Linux platform is explained in this paper. Further, the unified Bus-Monitor for number of aerospace project's configuration is developed and deployed on high performance processor architecture with optimized embedded computer. The development has been done for Hardware-In-Loop Simulation facility that is used for validation of avionics software

articleTitle: Investigating the Impact of Feedback Loop Training on Machine Learning Model's Performance in Time Series Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Current Trends in Advanced Computing (ICCTAC)
abstract: Ever since the development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML), the need for raw data has increased to mitigate this problem we investigate the impact of feedback loop training on an LSTM model's time series data and the performance of the model is investigated. We also employ traditional ML models like RandomForest Regression to perform a comparative study with the LSTM model. We seek to examine the effect on the accuracy and convergence behavior of the model by using its output as input for further iterations. A climate time-series dataset from Kaggle is used to train the LSTM model iteratively over ten iterations. According to our research, feedback loop training can have benefits like capturing intricate dependencies, but the cost outweighs the results as the model accuracy decreases drastically over several iterations of training. We have also compared the Model performance with traditional Machine Learning algorithms and other types of Neural Networks like ANNs.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Approaches for Emotion Recognition: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Current Trends in Advanced Computing (ICCTAC)
abstract: A key component that has arisen in[10] human-computer interaction, artificial intelligence, and affective computing is the ability to recognize emotions. The objective of the research project is to examine a method that is integrated for the recognition of facial expressions of emotion. Humans transmit their emotions through indirect and non-verbal means most of the time. Their sentiments are communicated through these methods. Providing a complete overview that includes an assessment of all the important emotion detection methods that can be found in a single region is the objective of the exposition that is now being presented. The paper represents the first attempt to offer an overview of all the emotion detection models that have been developed for the previous 10 years. The document contains an in-depth analysis of the technique as well as the datasets. For face identification, the technique makes use of the local Binary Pattern Histogram (LBPH), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) for feature extraction, and the Deep Face model for comprehensive emotion analysis.

articleTitle: The Evolution of Large Language Model: Models, Applications and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Current Trends in Advanced Computing (ICCTAC)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have attracted a lot of attention due to their success in natural language processing tasks. This paper provides a thorough overview by examining the architecture, applications, problems, assessment techniques, and future directions of LLM. With the constantly growing body of literature, a succinct yet comprehensive overview of recent developments is essential. Following the development of NLP, it highlights the move from rule-based systems to sophisticated transformer structures like as BERT and GPT. Important LLMs for text creation, translation, and summarization are mentioned, including T5, BART, and BioGPT. LLM performance is evaluated using metrics including as accuracy, perplexity, BLEU score, and ROUGE score. Research is still being done because of issues with bias, overfitting, and real-time processing. Future directions include managing longer contexts, lowering bias, and increasing efficiency through methods like federated learning. Continuous learning and multimodal LLMs are promising fields, as well as interpretive AI. In conclusion, LLMs have transformed natural language processing (NLP) and brought up both technical and ethical issues about the future of AI.

articleTitle: An Effective Framework of Iris Recognition Using UNet-Based Segmentation and Attention-Based Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Current Trends in Advanced Computing (ICCTAC)
abstract: Due to its numerous applications in security fields such as homeland security, border control, and airports, Iris Recognition (IR) has been a hotly debated field over the past few years. Despite the fact that many of the previous efforts at IR attain a very high rate of accuracy, a significant amount of preprocessing steps that are needed, and the use of handcrafted features make it inapplicable and ineffective for various datasets of the iris. Even though numerous types of research in this field of application are available, they still face numerous issues like complexity in computation and larger consumption of time. In this paper, a novel IR system is proposed to address the aforementioned issues. At first, the benchmark datasets are used to collect the raw iris images. Pre-processing is then performed on the collected images at the next phase using median filtering. The segmented images are obtained utilizing UNet from the resulting pre-processed image. Finally, the Attention-based ResNeXt (A-ResNeXt) method is used for the classification procedure. The performance is then calculated using a variety of parameters and is compared with other conventional approaches. As a result, the model's output undoubtedly demonstrates the improved recognition performance of the developed IR model.

articleTitle: Traffic Scene Text Detection for 3D Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Current Trends in Advanced Computing (ICCTAC)
abstract: With an emphasis on text localization, extraction, and recognition, this project outlines the development of an optical character recognition (OCR) system that makes use of the OpenCV (Open-Source Computer Vision) library. Text may be extracted from images, recognize it with OCR, and identify text portions utilizing OpenCV's image processing and analysis capabilities. With applications ranging from document digitization to image text extraction and data entry automation, the project's adaptability and accessibility make it a priceless tool for automating text-related tasks. This makes it a good choice for companies, researchers, and developers interested in OCR technology. By using OpenCV, the system's capabilities are enhanced, making it a more reliable and adaptable method for text extraction from images.

articleTitle: Customizing an Inference System to Extract Knowledge from Data Repositories Using Concepts of Fuzzy
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Current Trends in Advanced Computing (ICCTAC)
abstract: Algorithms are in abundance for extraction of information but some are not up to the expectation. It is due to the lack of effective mechanism in place to represent the required information. Fuzzy logic provides a sophisticated way of expressing the requirement with its membership functions, rule base and reasoning mechanisms. Membership function helps to flexibly specify the grade and extent of information needed and the rule base provides methods for combining them for effective representation of what is required. The reasoning mechanism in fuzzy logic helps to convert these representations into appropriate values so that the information can be classified according to our needs. In this research endeavour, a methodology has been delineated to describe the required information and a fuzzy model has been defined to extract the documents. It is flexible to change the required information and its extent using fuzzy logic. Using different types of rule sets how the extraction of information is being changed, has been discussed. Fuzzy inference system has been modelled to rank the documents in the order of the grade of information content. An algorithm has been provided to extract the information from rule sets. A generalized membership function has been delineated in this research work. By changing the parameter values in the membership function different membership functions can be initiated. By using two different sets of parameter values, two different membership functions have been modelled in this research work. These values combined with two different inference models namely, mamdani and sugeno models, totally four different fuzzy models have been implemented in this research work and the results are shown in the graphs at the end of this research work.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Impact of AI on Knowledge Acquisition of Students
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Current Trends in Advanced Computing (ICCTAC)
abstract: Education is a drawn-out process involving study, training, and teaching to acquire knowledge, skills, values, and habits. It fosters critical thinking, creativity, and problem-solving abilities. However, developing technology also impacts the education system by adopting specific methods; one of the important ones is artificial intelligence or AI. This paper investigates the transformative influence of AI-based tools on human creativity and problem-solving skills and the impacts on students than already existing conventional methods. A group of 126 students was considered as a part of the experiment to understand if there is any improvement in the explanation given by AI with modified commands and if there is any value addition in the level of knowledge of the students provided by AI with the frequency of AI usage. Wilcoxon Signed Rank Test, and Mann Whitney U Test difference tests were used to understand the quality improvement differences with repeated use of AI and the difference in knowledge acquisition between more and less frequent users. The results indicated that using AI showed an improvement with modified use. The frequency of AI use didn't significantly impact the students' existing knowledge. Significant progress in further knowledge acquisition was realized for students using AI more than three times a week. The study sheds light on the importance of the frequency of AI usage in maximizing its benefits for students, suggesting practical implications for integrating AI into educational settings.

articleTitle: A Cascaded Dynamic Attention-Based Deep Learning Model Segments Brain Tumors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Current Trends in Advanced Computing (ICCTAC)
abstract: Brain tumor diagnosis and treatment need segmentation, Precision automated segmentation of brain tumors is difficult due to their size, shape, unexpected placements, and fuzzy boundaries. U-Net is a popular medical picture segmentation model due to its simple architecture and high performance. Underutilized contextual information, limited local receptive fields, and lost spatial information are issues. For brain tumor segmentation, CDAU-Net, a novel model with Dynamic Convolution and Non-Local Attention Mechanism, addresses these issues. Two-stage cascaded three-dimensional U-Nets rebuild brain tumor spatial information at better resolution. The cascaded network's lateral connections receive maximal attention, improving its ability to collect long-distance interconnections and use tumor context information. Finally, dynamic convolutions with local adaptive capabilities replace normal convolutions in the cascaded network to increase local features capture. Extensive experiments were conducted on publicly available BraTS 2019 and 2020 datasets, comparing the proposed method with other representative approaches. Proposed method segments brain tumors. Brain tumor segmentation dice values of 0.897/0.903 for whole tumor, 0.826/0.828 for tumor core, and 0.781/0.786 for enhanced tumor segmentation worked in the BraTS 2019/2020 validation set.

articleTitle: Leveraging Customer Sentiment Analysis with Deep Learning for Business Growth Forecasting and Product Flaw Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Current Trends in Advanced Computing (ICCTAC)
abstract: This study harnesses Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) alongside advanced Deep Learning models such as Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Bidirectional LSTM (bi-LSTM), and ResNet, incorporating Time Series Analysis and Word2Vec embeddings for sophisticated customer sentiment analysis within business contexts. We introduce a novel CNN-based framework that integrates these methodologies to simultaneously forecast business growth and identify product flaws, utilizing large-scale datasets comprising customer reviews, feedback, and social media data. By capturing hidden patterns and nuances within text data, our framework transcends traditional sentiment analysis, providing actionable insights for informed decision-making. Through rigorous evaluation, including the application of Time Series Analysis for predicting future sales trends, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework in facilitating customer acquisition and pinpointing areas for product improvement. These findings underscore its potential to optimize market performance and drive product development strategies in dynamic business landscapes.

articleTitle: Schizophrenia Detection using Electroencephalography Signals Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Current Trends in Advanced Computing (ICCTAC)
abstract: The objective of the project is to see whether deep learning can be used to identify schizophrenia in teenagers by analysing their EEG data. The work takes advantage of both conventional and novel preprocessing techniques, such as the Short-Time Fourier Transform, to extract characteristic signals associated with schizophrenia from EEG data. The study highlights encouraging results with models including VGG-16, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)[24], and Pyramidal Spatial-based Feature Attention Network (PSFAN). Notably, PSFAN presents a novel diagnostic methodology that extracts multiscale features from 4-second EEG recordings and converts them into 2-dimensional images using dilated convolutions. On two datasets, custom CNN shows statistical superiority over eleven state-of-the-art algorithms through subject-dependent, subject-independent, and cross-dataset experiments [16]. This paper highlights the usefulness of deep learning in medical settings and highlights its potential.

articleTitle: Feature Selection in Ozone Feature Space Impacts Performance in Gradient Boosting, Random Forest, Xgboost and Adaptive Boosting Regressors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Current Trends in Advanced Computing (ICCTAC)
abstract: This study investigated the efficacy of feature selection methods in enhancing ozone prediction through regression models, utilizing the “AQBench” dataset, abundant with air quality indicators and environmental variables. We focused on Adaptive Boosting, Gradient Boost Regressor, Random Forest Regressor, and XGBoost Regressor, assessing the impact of various feature selection strategies—such as Feature Shuffling, Random Forest Importance, and Step-Forward Feature Selection—on model performance. Our findings highlighted that the XGBoost Regressor stood out for its accuracy and generalizability across different feature selection methods, emphasizing the critical role of targeted feature selection in environmental predictive modeling. This research contributes to integrating machine learning techniques in environmental science, providing insights that could influence public health and policy decisions. It underscores the potential of computational approaches to enhance air quality forecasts, paving the way for future investigations into additional models and datasets to refine environmental predictive analytics.

articleTitle: VisioGuide: Modified YoloV7 with ResNext for Object Detection to Aid Visually Impaired Individuals
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Current Trends in Advanced Computing (ICCTAC)
abstract: People with visual impairment face multiple unique challenges in navigating and interacting with their surroundings. As the demand for revolutionary assistive technology grows to improve the movability of visually impaired people, Deep learning has emerged as a key solution. The need of revolutionary assistive technology made to improve the mobility and independence of visually disabled people is increasing by each passing day. Using the YOLOv7 object detection algorithm along with a few modifications in its backbone, Visioguide deploys deep learning algorithms to accurately detect and identify real-time objects, landmarks, and points of interest in real-time, thereby enabling seamless navigation and heightened spatial awareness for its users. The enhancements in YoloV7 backbone using weight initialization and spatial attention have increased the efficiency of object detection for visually impaired individuals. This robust technology serves as an indispensable aid, thereby making the visually impaired feel a part of the society and helping them to perform their daily chores. The paper proposes an efficient approach to object detection using modified YoloV7 along with voice feedback to aid visually impaired individual. The model is effective and convenient to detect general objects with mAP value of 59.2%. The paper proposes a study of YoloV7 object detection using modified ResNext Backbone Architecture and voice feedback of detected class.

articleTitle: Towards a Model: Exploring Fatigue Factors in ZOOM Online Classes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Current Trends in Advanced Computing (ICCTAC)
abstract: The ascent of Zoom as the predominant platform for facilitating online classes signifies a notable paradigm shift in the domain of remote education. Its rapid adoption can be attributed to several factors, such as its intuitive interface, robust technological infrastructure, and adaptability across various educational contexts. Against the backdrop of the global pandemic, which has mandated a widespread transition to remote learning, Zoom has emerged as a pivotal tool for educators endeavoring to transcend geographical constraints and engage with students in virtual classrooms. Its pervasive presence has reshaped pedagogical approaches, facilitating interactive and collaborative learning experiences irrespective of geographical boundaries. This study examines the correlations between visual fatigue, physical fatigue, mental fatigue, tech-savvy behavior, and online learning among 724 teachers in Karnataka conducting online classes through Zoom. The survey, administered from January to June 2023, utilized purposive sampling. Rigorous data analysis comprised factor loadings, Cronbach's alpha, Rho_A, CR, HTMT ratio, Fornell-Larcker Criterion, assessments of multicollinearity, R square, path coefficients, and predictive validity, employing Smart PLS software.

articleTitle: TransVOD: Transformer-Based Visual Object Detection for Self-Driving Cars
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Current Trends in Advanced Computing (ICCTAC)
abstract: Detection of the objects using various models and technologies is performed within the domain of computer vision. This has an application in the medical industry, automation, and self-driving car industries, among many others. It is predicted that by the year 2025 there will be over 8 million self-driving cars running on roads. According to studies, by 2050 almost all cars and public transportation will be automated. Object detection is an essential and one of the most important tasks for self-driving cars. It allows the vehicle to sense and navigate their environment in a safe and efficient manner. This involves identifying and locating a variety of things in the car's field of vision including traffic lights, road signals, pedestrians and other cars. The goal of this research is to investigate and evaluate the issues that arise when autonomous automobiles use their visual subsystem to identify things. This paper proposes a unique custom Detection Transformer model for visual object detection in autonomous vehicles, specifically addressing the limitations of pre-trained models such as reduced accuracy for small objects and slower processing times. The study incorporates a self-attention mechanism that occurs after the DETR backbone has extracted features. Using an attention mechanism in the model will enhance the DETR's performance on the custom dataset. The proposed model achieves a 20% improvement in accuracy for detecting small objects compared to pre-trained models and can detect up to 100 objects per second with over 90% accuracy. These findings suggest that the proposed model can significantly enhance the performance of object detection applications in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Transformer Based Text Summary Generation for Videos
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Current Trends in Advanced Computing (ICCTAC)
abstract: With advancements in the multimedia sector, abundant videos are being generated for several applications. Consequently, video summarization has emerged as a crucial endeavor, aimed at distilling key segments from videos while preserving essential information. Furthermore, the ability to comprehend video content and autonomously generate event synopses holds significant potential for streamlining the creation of video descriptions, thereby alleviating the manual efforts typically required for this task. In this paper, a Transformer-based Video-to-text generator is proposed that can generate a concise summary for videos containing frequent scene changes. The proposed pipeline involves the identification of keyframes from the input videos and the extraction of images. Evaluation is done on a custom dataset, and the average BLEU 4 and ROGUE-f-measures obtained are 50.69% and 37.78% respectively. These results outperform the CNN- LSTM video-to-text summarization approach and highlight the robustness of Transformers.

articleTitle: Blockchain Based Toll Collection System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Current Trends in Advanced Computing (ICCTAC)
abstract: In the era of interstitial tax challenges, lack of area, inefficiencies, and an orchestra of fraud, a phoenix of reform appears in which the Ethereum-based blockchain technology acts as a warrior to prevent frauds and misconception. This research, now not most effective, may require some extra innovations and technology implies the essence of blockchain to reconsider toll management system. In the view of interstitial tax annoying conditions, lack of location, inefficiencies, and web of frauds, a phoenix of reforms like Ethereum will be the saviour for the same. This research emphasizes the significant shift towards using blockchain technology to enhance data integrity and decentralization of data. By decentralizing power and ensuring immutability, it aims to promote transparency and reliability in data management. This new system functions like the intricate web of a spider, using blockchain's decentralized structure to smoothly manage the workflow. It elegantly handles the complexities of maintaining data integrity. Real-time audits may not be longer just be a display, but a practical feature that can be utilized effectively. This propped system will act as a spider web technology of blockchain decentralized system which enables flawless transparency, maintains data integrity and will be user friendly. Ethereum will be the revolution changer with all the requisite tools and infrastructure for the implementation of this blockchain-powered toll collection system. Beyond the problematic rectification of existing issues, Ethereum expansion will extend to the realms of data analytics, smart contracts, and the decentralized networks of transactions.

articleTitle: Driver Monitoring based on Drowsiness and Yawning using YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Current Trends in Advanced Computing (ICCTAC)
abstract: The Samruddhi Mahamarg, a vital expressway, witnesses numerous accidents each year due to driving hypnosis and drowsiness, especially on its long stretches. This thesis proposes a novel approach to enhance safety by addressing these issues through the identification of drowsy eyes and yawning using state-of-the-art deep learning models. The system employs two YOLOv8 models, one dedicated to detecting drowsy eyes and the other for recognizing yawning behavior. Remarkably high accuracy rates of 99.92% for drowsy eyes and 99.95% for yawning demonstrate the robustness and reliability of the proposed models. By accurately identifying these critical signs of driver fatigue, the system provides timely alerts, mitigating the risks associated with driving hypnosis. This research emphasizes the importance of mitigating driving hypnosis to reduce the frequency of accidents on highways like Samruddhi Mahamarg, emphasizing the potential to save lives and prevent injuries. The incorporation of cutting-edge technology in real-time monitoring showcases the commitment to advancing road safety in high-risk environments.

articleTitle: Integrated Sensory Perception: Real-Time Object Detection, Action Recognition and Emotion Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Current Trends in Advanced Computing (ICCTAC)
abstract: - This research study presents a comprehensive approach to emotion recognition leveraging a combination of object detection, action recognition, and emotion recognition models, integrated with Kinect sensors for accurate mapping in low-light environments. The model achieves a combined precision and recall range of 82-85%, demonstrating its effectiveness in identifying objects and emotions. Object detection is performed using YOLO, action recognition utilizing LSTM, and emotion recognition employing CNN. Additionally, low-light robustness is ensured through the incorporation of a Zero-DCE model. A unique dataset for training the model under low-light conditions is generated using Kinect sensors. The methodology involves rigorous analysis of behavior, encompassing object detection and tracking methods, gesture and emotion recognition, data preprocessing, and feature extraction. Findings indicate that YOLO-based tracking approaches significantly enhance emotion recognition systems. This study contributes to advancing behavior analysis by highlighting the efficacy of various object tracking techniques. particularly in low-light environments.
